He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt Commodores]]. ==Early life== Lee grew up in [[Phoenix, Arizona]] and attended [[Corona del Sol High School]] in [[Tempe, Arizona]]. As a junior, Lee was named first-team All-State after averaging 18 points, five rebounds, and three assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/recruiting/2016/6/1/11816360/arizona-basketball-recruiting-in-state-prospect-saben-lees-recruitment-heating-up|title=Arizona basketball recruiting: In-state prospect Saben Lee's recruitment heating up|first=Alec|last=Sills-Trausch|website=AZDesertSwarm.com|date=June 1, 2016}} Lee committed to play college basketball at Vanderbilt after his junior year over offers from Louisville, Stanford, Florida State, and Nebraska.{{cite web|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2016/06/14/corona-del-sol-pg-saben-lee-commits-vanderbilt/85867166/|title=Corona Del Sol PG Saben Lee commits to Vanderbilt|work=[[The Arizona Republic]]}}{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2646167-saben-lee-to-vanderbilt-commodores-land-4-star-pg-prospect|title=Saben Lee to Vanderbilt: Commodores Land 4-Star PG Prospect|first=Danny|last=Webster|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=June 14, 2016}} He was again named first team All-State as a senior and scored 39 points against [[Cesar Chavez High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|Cesar Chavez High School]] in the state semifinal to lead the Aztecs to the state title game before falling to [[Basha High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.prephoops.com/2017/03/arizona-6a-state/|title=Arizona 6A All-State|first=Jordan|last=Augustine|website=PrepHoops.com|date=October 22, 2017}}{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/corona-del-sol-returns-to-final-behind-saben-lees-39-points-will-meet-basha-for-6a-boys-crown|title=Corona del Sol returns to final behind Saben Lee's 39 points, will meet Basha for 6A boys crown|first=Richard|last=Obert|website=USATodayHSS.com|date=February 24, 2017}} ==College career== Lee served as the Commodores starting point guard as a true freshman and averaged 10.6 points, 3.1 assists and a team-leading 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web|url=https://sports.usatoday.com/2018/10/03/vanderbilt-basketballs-darius-garland-saben-lee-working-on-chemistry/|title=Vanderbilt basketball's Darius Garland, Saben Lee working on chemistry|first=Adam|last=Sparks|website=[[USAToday.com]]|publisher=[[Nashville Tennessean]]|date=October 3, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2020|archive-date=June 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624103902/https://sports.usatoday.com/2018/10/03/vanderbilt-basketballs-darius-garland-saben-lee-working-on-chemistry/|url-status=dead}} As a sophomore, Lee averaged 12.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 1.0 steals per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.tnledger.com/editorial/article.aspx?id=115302|title=Vanderbilt's Lee making the most of challenging season|first=Ivan|last=Aronin|work=The Nashville Ledger|date=March 8, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2019/09/01/sec-basketball-top-returning-players-team-2019-20-season/2/|title=SEC Basketball: Top returning players on each team for 2019–20 season|first=Charlie|last=DiSturco|website=BustingBrackets.com|date=September 2019|publisher=[[FanSided]]}} As a junior, he averaged 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.5 steals per game and was named second team All-SEC by the [[Associated Press]].{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2880701-sec-2020-final-team-standings-top-player-stats-and-best-nba-draft-prospects|title=SEC 2020 Final Team Standings, Top Player Stats and Best NBA Draft magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/vanderbilt/basketball/vanderbilts-saben-lee-scottie-pippen-jr-honored-by-sec|title=Vanderbilt's Saben Lee, Scottie Pippen Jr. Honored By SEC|first=Greg|last=Arias|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=March 9, 2020}} He scored a career high 38 points on March 3, 2020, in an 87–79 win over [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166380|title=Lee's 38 leads Vanderbilt to 87–79 upset of Alabama|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 3, 2020}} Following the end of the season, Lee declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2020/03/27/saben-lee-declares-nba-draft-vanderbilt-basketball/2926329001/|title=Vanderbilt guard Saben Lee declares for NBA Draft|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=March 27, 2020|access-date=March 28, 2020}} On May 1, he announced he was signing with an agent and forgoing his last season of eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Weinstein |first1=Robbie |title=Vanderbilt's Saben Lee signs with agent, will stay in NBA Draft |url=https://247sports.com/college/vanderbilt/Article/Vanderbilt-Commodores-Saben-Lee-signs-with-agent-will-stay-in-NBA-Draft-146718540/ |access-date=May 3, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=May 1, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2020–2022)=== Lee was selected 38th overall by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2020 NBA draft]], then subsequently traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] on November 22, 2020.{{cite news |last1=Sparks |first1=Adam |title=Vanderbilt's Saben Lee drafted with No. 38 pick in NBA Draft, headed to Detroit via trade |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/vanderbilt/2020/11/18/saben-lee-nba-draft-detroit-pistons-38-overall-pick-vanderbilt/6305608002/ |access-date=November 18, 2020 |work=[[The Tennessean]] |date=November 18, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-cash-considerations|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Cash Considerations|work=NBA.com|date=November 22, 2020|access-date=November 22, 2020}} On December 1, 2020, the [[Detroit Pistons]] signed him to a two-way contract with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Sign Rookies Killian Hayes, Isaiah Stewart, Saddiq Bey and Saben Lee|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-rookies-killian-hayes-isaiah-stewart-saddiq-bey-and-saben-lee|date=December 1, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 1, 2020}}{{cite web|last1=Gauruder|first1=Dana|title=Pistons To Sign Saben Lee To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/11/pistons-to-sign-saben-lee-to-two-way-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors|date=November 18, 2020|access-date=March 30, 2021}} On May 11, 2021, Lee scored a career-high 22 points in a 119–100 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. On August 6, 2021, the Pistons re-signed Lee to a multi-year contract.{{Cite web |title=Saben Lee Re-Signs With Pistons |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/saben-lee-to-re-sign-with-pistons.html |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} On April 1, 2022, Lee achieved his first career [[double-double]], with 11 points and 12 assists in a 110–101 win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. ===Raptors 905 (2022)=== On September 26, 2022, Lee was traded with [[Kelly Olynyk]] to the [[Utah Jazz]] for [[Bojan Bogdanović]].{{cite web|first=Angie|last=Treasure|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Kelly Olynyk, Saben Lee, and Cash Considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-kelly-olynyk-saben-lee-and-cash-considerations|website=NBA.com|publisher=Utah Jazz|date=September 26, 2022|access-date=September 27, 2022}} He was waived by the Jazz on October 9.{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Sign Darryl Morsell |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-darryl-morsell |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On October 11, Lee signed an exhibit 10 contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=SUNS SIGN ARMS, LEE |url=https://twitter.com/geraldbourguet/status/1580002364823461888 |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Twitter |language=en}} He was waived on October 13.{{Cite web |title=SUNS WAIVE ARMS, LEE, LUWAWU-CABARROT |url=https://twitter.com/geraldbourguet/status/1581405067453734912 |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Twitter |language=en}} On October 16, Lee signed an exhibit 10 contract with the [[Toronto Raptors]], but was waived the same day.{{Cite web |title=Raptors Sign, Waive Saben Lee |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/10/raptors-sign-waive-saben-lee.html |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}} On October 18, Lee joined the [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA G League]]. ===Philadelphia 76ers (2022)=== On November 23, 2022, Lee signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], replacing [[Michael Foster Jr.]] on a [[two-way contract]].{{Cite web |title=Saben Lee Signs Two-Way Contract with Sixers |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/saben-lee-signed-to-two-way-contract-with-76ers |access-date=November 23, 2022 |website=nba.com}} On December 26, he was waived in favor of [[Louis King (basketball)|Louis King]].{{cite web |date=December 26, 2022 |title=Louis King Signed to Two-Way Deal |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/louis-king-signed-to-two-way-contract-with-76ers |access-date=December 26, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ===Return to the 905 (2022–2023)=== On December 28, 2022, Lee was re-acquired by the [[Raptors 905]].{{Cite tweet |user=@Raptors905 |number=1608529239682293761 |title=Got our guy back Welcome back, Saben}} ===Phoenix Suns (2023–2024)=== On January 11, 2023, Lee signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=OFFICIAL: Phoenix Suns sign Saben Lee to a 10-day contract. |url=https://twitter.com/suns/status/1613302208870912000 |access-date=2023-01-11 |website=Twitter |language=en}} He signed a second 10-day contract with the Suns on January 21.{{Cite web |title=Suns Sign Saben Lee To Second 10-Day Contract |url=https://twitter.com/geraldbourguet/status/1616848485034360835 |access-date=2023-01-22 |website=Twitter |language=en}} Lee signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Suns on February 1.{{Cite web |title=Duane Rankin on Twitter: "#Suns re-sign Saben Lee to two-way, waive Duane Washington Jr., who was on a two-way deal." |url=https://twitter.com/DuaneRankin/status/1620931693740986369?cxt=HHwWgsDUqbKy2v4sAAAA |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=Twitter}} He was named to the G League's inaugural Next Up Game for the 2022–23 season.{{Cite web |title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game |access-date=March 8, 2023 |website=NBA G League}} During the final game of the regular season, Lee recorded his second double-double of his NBA career (first with the Suns) with a career-high 25 points and 10 rebounds in a 119–114 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on April 9, 2023.{{Cite web |title=Clippers vs Suns, April 9, 2023 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202304090PHO.html |access-date=2024-07-02 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} On July 13, 2023, Lee signed another two-way contract with the Suns.{{cite web|title=SUNS RE-SIGN SABEN LEE|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-re-sign-saben-lee|website=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2023|access-date=July 14, 2023}} ===Manisa Basket (2024)=== On August 30, 2024, Lee signed with [[Manisa Basket]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]].{{cite Instagram|user=manisabasket94|title=🇬🇧:🚨 Saben Lee joins Manisa Basket! 🚨 With his NBA experience, speed, and scoring prowess, Saben Lee is set to make a huge impact on our team this season. 💪 Ready to leave his mark on both ends of the court, Manisa's new star is here! 🌟 Are you ready to share the excitement and live this new season together? 🏀🔥 Welcome to the Manisa Basket family, @_sabenlee 🙌|postid=C_S5WqDoIy-|date=August 30, 2024|access-date=September 18, 2024}} He would only play in one game for Manisa Basket before leaving the team. ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2024)=== On October 13, 2024, Lee signed with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web|title=Maccabi adds scorer Saben Lee|url=https://maccabi.co.il/news.asp?id=20360&lang=en|website=Maccabi.co.il|publisher=[[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]|date=October 13, 2024|access-date=October 13, 2024}} He signed a two-year contract.{{cite web|title=Saben Lee officially joins Maccabi Tel Aviv|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1727336/saben-lee-officially-joins-maccabi-tel-aviv/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=October 13, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2024}} ===Return to Manisa Basket (2024–2025)=== On November 23, 2024, Lee returned to [[Manisa Basket]] after struggling to settle in Maccabi.{{cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1746417/saben-lee-reportedly-leaving-maccabi-tel-aviv-to-return-to-manisa/|title=Saben Lee reportedly leaving Maccabi Tel Aviv to return to Manisa|website=eurohoops.net|date=November 22, 2024}} ===Olympiacos (2025)=== On February 27, 2025, Lee signed with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] of the [[Greek Basket League|Greek Basketball League]] (GBL).{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/official-olympiacos-signs-saben-lee-until-2027/|title=Olympiacos signs Saben Lee until 2027|last=|first=|date=February 27, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=February 28, 2025}} He signed until the end of the 2026–27 season.{{cite web |title=Saben Lee signs with Olympiacos until the end of the 2026-27 season |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1790813/saben-lee-signs-with-olympiacos-until-the-end-of-the-2026-27-season/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=28 February 2025 |language=en |date=27 February 2025}} ===Anadolu Efes (2025–2026)=== On December 29, 2025, Lee signed a remainder of the season contract with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web |title=Saben Lee leaves Reds, links up with Efes |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/saben-lee-leaves-reds-links-up-with-efes/ |website=EuroLeague |access-date=29 December 2025 |language=en |date=29 December 2025}} On June 9, 2026, Anadolu Efes announced that it had parted ways with Lee following the conclusion of the 2025–26 season.{{cite web |title=Anadolu Efes parts ways with Saben Lee and Cole Swider |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1978669/anadolu-efes-parts-ways-with-saben-lee-and-cole-swider/ |website=Eurohoops |date=9 June 2026 |access-date=10 June 2026}} ===Žalgiris Kaunas (2026–present)=== On June 16, 2026, Lee signed a two–year contract with [[BC Žalgiris|Zalgiris Kaunas]] of the
